items.title: Section: Even Craving a Reputation for Few Desires Is Still Covetousness

items.zh: 又依七事而發綺語。謂鬪訟諍競語、諸婆羅門惡呪術語、苦所逼語、戲笑遊樂之語、處眾雜語、顛狂語、邪命語，如是一切名綺語罪。復次，若於家主起如是欲：云何我當同於家主，領諸僕使，隨欲所作。是名貪欲。又起是欲：即彼家主所有父母、妻子、奴婢及諸作使，廣說乃至七攝受事、十資身事，謂飲食等，皆當屬我。又起是欲：云何令他知我少欲、知足、遠離、勇猛精進，安住正念、寂定、聰慧，諸漏永盡，施戒多聞。又起是欲：云何令他供養於我。謂諸國王乃至商主，若苾芻、苾芻尼、鄔波索迦、鄔波斯迦等，皆當恭敬、尊重、承事、供養於我。
items.en: Idle chatter also arises through seven grounds: speech of dispute and contention, the evil spell-talk of brahmins, speech driven by suffering, speech of play and amusement, mixed idle talk among a crowd, deranged speech, and speech of wrong livelihood — all of this is the offence of idle chatter. Moreover, if one serving a master forms this wish: how might I become like my master, commanding servants, doing as I wish — this is covetousness. Also forming this wish: that master's own parents, spouse, servants, and workers, and in full the seven kinds of holdings and ten kinds of life's necessities, food and drink and the rest, should all belong to me. Also forming this wish: how might others know me as one of few desires, contentment, seclusion, vigorous diligence, settled mindfulness, calm stability, and wisdom, outflows exhausted, giving, disciplined, and learned. Also forming this wish: how might others make offerings to me — kings and merchants, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen alike revering, honouring, serving, and making offerings to me.

items.title: Section: Eight Forms of Covetousness Complete, and Malice Begins With Revenge

items.zh: 又起是欲：云何令我當得利養、衣服、飲食、諸坐臥具、病緣醫藥及資生具。又起是欲：云何令我當生天上，天妙五欲以為遊戲。又起是欲：云何令我當生魯達羅世界、毘瑟笯世界，人中希有眾同分中，乃至令我當生他化自在眾同分中。又起是欲：云何令我乃至當得父母、妻子、奴婢、作使、朋友、宰官、親戚、兄弟、同梵行等所有資產。如是一切，皆名貪欲業道所攝。若作是思：彼於我所有無義欲，故我於彼當作無義。是名瞋恚。又作是思：彼於我所已作、正作、當作無義，我亦於彼當作無義。亦名瞋恚。
items.en: Also forming this wish: how might I obtain profit, clothing, food and drink, bedding, and medicine for illness. Also forming this wish: how might I be reborn in the heavens, enjoying the exquisite five heavenly pleasures. Also forming this wish: how might I be reborn in the world of Rudra, the world of Viṣṇu, among rare and eminent humankind, or even among those who freely enjoy what others transform. Also forming this wish: how might I obtain the parents, spouse, servants, workers, friends, officials, relatives, siblings, or fellow renunciants belonging to another. All of this belongs to the karma-path of covetousness. If one thinks: he wants to do me harm, so I shall do him harm in return — this is malice.

items.title: Section: Nine Grounds of Malice Complete — All Ten Karma-Paths' Methods Now Closed

items.zh: 如是廣說九惱害事，當知亦爾。又作是思：云何令我於能損害怨家惡友而得自在，縛害驅擯，或行鞭撻，或散財產，或奪妻妾、朋友、眷屬及家宅等。此惱害心亦名瞋恚。又起是思：云何令彼能損於我怨家惡友，於他處所遭如上說諸苦惱事。此損害心亦名瞋恚。又作是思：願彼自然發起如是如是身語意行，由此喪失資財、朋友、眷屬、名稱、安樂、受命及諸善法，身壞當生諸惡趣中。如是一切惱害之心，皆名瞋恚根本業道。復次，若作是思：決定無施。是名邪見。廣說乃至謗因、謗用、謗果，壞真善事，如是一切皆名邪見根本業道。
items.en: As broadly explained, the nine grounds of ill will should be understood likewise. Also forming this thought: how might I gain mastery over my enemies and ill-wishing companions, binding, harming, expelling, or beating them, scattering their wealth, or seizing their spouse, friends, family, and home — this mind of ill will is also malice. Also forming this thought: how might my enemies and ill-wishing companions suffer the aforesaid misfortunes at another's hands. This mind of harm is also malice. Also forming this thought: may they spontaneously engage in such conduct of body, speech, and mind, thereby losing wealth, friends, family, reputation, happiness, life, and every wholesome dharma, and upon the body's destruction, fall into the evil destinies. Every such mind of ill will is the root karma-path of malice. Moreover, if one thinks, there is certainly no giving, this is wrong view. Broadly speaking, denying cause, denying function, denying result, and destroying what is genuinely real, all of this is the root karma-path of wrong view.

items.title: Section: Why This One Denial Is Singled Out as "Wrong View"

items.zh: 問：一切倒見皆名邪見，何故世尊於業道中，但說如是誹謗之見名為邪見？答：由此邪見，諸邪見中最為殊勝。何以故？由此邪見為依止故，有一沙門、若婆羅門斷諸善根。又此邪見最順惡業。懷邪見者，於諸惡法隨意所行，是故此見偏說在彼惡業道中。當知餘見非不邪見自相相應。
items.en: Question: every distorted view is called wrong view — why does the Blessed One, within the karma-paths, speak only of this slandering view as wrong view? Answer: because this wrong view is the most extreme among all wrong views. Why so? Because, relying on this wrong view, a certain ascetic or brahmin severs every wholesome root. Also, this wrong view most closely accords with unwholesome karma. One who holds wrong view acts as they wish among every unwholesome dharma, and for this reason this view is specifically said to belong among the unwholesome karma-paths. It should be known that every other view is not thereby excluded from being genuinely wrong view in its own right.

blocks.text: A short day: the subtle forms of covetousness and malice, and why one wrong view is singled out as the worst.

Master Cháng Bǎi: pressed by pain, one chatters meaninglessly; people chat about worldly pleasures instead of practising. Even wanting others to know how few one's desires are is covetousness; compare Day 531: the truly content do not want to be known.
Master Cháng Bǎi: enjoying heavenly pleasures is also covetousness. And malice begins with revenge: "he wants to harm me, so I should do the same to him."
Master Cháng Bǎi: wishing that others harm him, or that he himself act badly and be ruined, are also malice.
Master Cháng Bǎi: it is the strongest in destructive force, severing wholesome roots and leaving one reckless in every evil.
Affliction completed, karma begun. The ten courses of action are analysed with legal precision, but the point is inward: intention, motive, and satisfaction decide the weight of every deed.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain speech under suffering, crowd talk, and wrong-livelihood speech?
options: prayers for the sick, sermons, and fortune-telling, all beneficial if informal
all outsider spells
all sūtra speech
words without thought under pain; idle talk with no practice in it; flattery for livelihood
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: pressed by pain, one speaks meaninglessly without thought; people chat idly about worldly pleasures instead of practice; flattering untruths are spoken to win support. Four other kinds of idle chatter in the source are missing from the English.

quiz.q: Is wishing others to know one has few desires still covetousness?
options: no: fewness of desires is good and telling others encourages them, the passage praising it, as the lecture holds
only for monastics
yes: the very thought is the path of covetousness, already joined with evil
only when spoken
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if the mind stirs with such a thought, it is covetousness, the path itself, already joined with evil. Compare §21: the truly few-desired do not seek to be known. A sharp point on reputation for humility.

quiz.q: The English has "how might I obtain the parents, spouse..." What is left out?
options: it omits 資產: what is coveted is these persons' property, not the persons
nothing: it means obtaining the people, 資產 being filler, as above
it omits 云何
it omits 當得
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi explicitly says the property these people own. The English stops at the list and adds "belonging to another," turning a wish for their assets into a wish for the persons. The same section also drops 資生具 from the list of requisites.

quiz.q: Is wishing for rebirth in heaven or Rudra's world covetousness?
options: no: it is a wholesome wish, heavenly results being good, only wishing others' wealth counting
yes: all belong to covetousness's path, a craving for future existence
only Rudra's
only the Paranirmita heaven
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: enjoying heavenly sense pleasures is also covetousness; the delight of enjoying what others transform is a craving for further existence, and part of this path. So the object can be religious yet still be covetous. The English keeps Rudra and Viṣṇu.

quiz.q: The English has "he wishes me ill without cause, so I shall wish him ill in return." What is the problem?
options: no problem: 無義 means without reason, and 當作 only a wish
the problem is "he"
the problem is "me"
無義 means harm, not "without cause"; 當作 means doing, not merely wishing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: he wants to do what is bad for me, so I should answer tooth for tooth and do what is bad for him. 無義 is harm. "Without cause" adds an idea of injustice the Chinese lacks, and "wish" softens 當作. The source's sentence on past, present, and future harm is also lost.

quiz.q: How are malice's three thoughts distinguished?
options: all three wish the enemy well, returning good for evil, the passage urging conversion of anger, with no path established
harming oneself; wishing others to harm; wishing the enemy's own deeds to ruin them
all concern the past
all concern the higher realms
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the second is not harming personally but wishing that others harm him; the third, if neither I nor others harm him, is wishing that he himself act badly and be ruined. The treatise covers every form of ill will, so malice completes in thought alone.

quiz.q: The English has "the most excellent among all wrong views." What is the problem?
options: 殊勝 means most extreme; "excellent" is praise, the reverse; the lecture says worst, most destructive
no problem: 殊勝 means best, this being the most complete theory
the problem is "among"
the problem is "wrong views"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it is the worst among wrong views, with the strongest destructive force, severing wholesome roots, leaving one reckless in every evil. 殊勝 means foremost in degree. "Most excellent" would praise it; "most extreme" or "gravest" is needed. Other distorted views are still wrong views.
